hook: Advice from the oldest book in the world
hook_sub: Written in Egypt 4,000 years ago. Still true.

slides.t: Don't be proud because you know a lot. Talk with the ordinary person as you would with the expert.
Nobody has ever reached the limit of a skill. No craftsman is ever done learning.
Good words are rarer than emeralds, yet you may hear them from a servant at the grindstone.
Ptahhotep, chief minister to an Egyptian king. These are his first words to his son.

slides.t: Follow your heart as long as you live. Don't do more than is required.
Don't cut short the time for enjoying life. Wasting it is hateful.
Don't work longer than you need to keep your household.
When you have enough, enjoy it. Wealth is useless to a man who is worn out.

hook_sub: Three rules from the oldest book in the world

slides.t: Lower your arms. Don't get angry when he disagrees. Your calm will win the argument for you.
If he says something wrong, don't stay silent. Speak up, and people will respect you.
Never bully him. Leave him alone and he will trip over his own words.
How you treat people with less power shows your real character. True then, true now.

hook: Greed was called a disease 4,000 years ago
hook_sub: The vizier Ptahhotep, to his son

slides.t: Beware of greed. It is a painful disease with no cure.
It sets in-laws against each other and drives husbands and wives apart.
What goes into the storeroom must come out again. Bread is meant to be shared.
It is a man's kindness that is remembered after he is gone.

hook: How to test a friend, ancient Egypt
hook_sub: From the oldest book in the world

slides.t: To know what a friend is really like, don't ask his companions.
Sit with him yourself. After a while, talk and test his heart in conversation.
Don't be cold, don't answer with scorn, and don't interrupt before he has finished.
When he tells you about his life, you'll know whether to keep him close.

hook: The one who listens is listened to
hook_sub: The most famous line of Ptahhotep

slides.t: Listening is better than anything. It creates goodwill.
In Egyptian, the same word meant 'to hear' and 'to obey'. Listening was respect.
Let your heart be generous, but hold back your tongue.
Teach your children what is true and just, as your father taught you.
